stories.title: Sources: Mike McCarthy has Steelers' full support after Aaron Rodgers interview
stories.summary: Mike McCarthy has the full support of the Steelers organization and will remain the team's coach after Aaron Rodgers' allegations, sources told NFL Network and ESPN.
stories.detail: PITTSBURGH -- Mike McCarthy has the full support of the Pittsburgh Steelers organization and will remain the team's coach after Aaron Rodgers ' stunning allegations Wednesday, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Sources told Rapoport and Fowler that the Steelers are standing by McCarthy in the wake of Rodgers' bombshell interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" in which the star quarterback accused the longtime coach of sleeping through team meetings. Multiple sources around the NFL corroborated Rodgers' account of McCarthy to ESPN reporters, with one saying: "It's all true." "Obviously we talk regularly, so they're very in tune with everything that goes on in football operations as far as my job responsibility," McCarthy said of ownership and front office involvement in the decision to bench and then release the four-time MVP. "And I think they do a very good job of communicating back and forth. And so it was clearly my decision, and they have supported me 100%." stories.title: What's next for Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy, Steelers?
stories.summary: The news out of Pittsburgh shook the NFL landscape, and ESPN's insiders share insights on the QB, the coach and their futures.
stories.detail: The Pittsburgh Steelers went from a 6-4 team vying for playoff contention with a four-time MVP quarterback under center Tuesday to a team entering its Week 12 game Friday against the Denver Broncos reeling from controversy and now without Aaron Rodgers on its roster. Pittsburgh waived Rodgers after the quarterback said Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he wouldn't return to the team after his stunning benching Tuesday night . It was a scorched-earth interview that included allegations that coach Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through team meetings , among other embarrassing details. Rodgers said he found out from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched and still hasn't heard the news from McCarthy. The veteran quarterback and the coach's partnership goes back to when they were together in Green Bay as the Packers won Super Bowl XLV and extended to McCarthy being fired eight years later in 2018. Turning 43 on Sunday, Rodgers had known limitations entering the 2026 season. stories.title: Rams' Kam Kinchens ejected as hit leaves Packers' Christian Watson concussed
stories.summary: Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for a hit along the sideline that left Packers wide receiver Christian Watson with a concussion Wednesday night.
stories.detail: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for a hit along the sideline that left Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson with a concussion Wednesday night. The play came on a fourth-and-1 play late in the second quarter, when Kinchens left his feet and launched into Watson while leading with his head. Watson was down long enough that medical personnel came across the field with a gurney, but it was not needed. Watson got up and walked to the locker room. He was ruled out because of the concussion at the start of the second half. Kinchens initially was called for unnecessary roughness, then was ejected after a video review. He reached a maximum speed of 18.41 mph on the play, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Kinchens is the first Rams player disqualified from a game since Puka Nacua was ejected in Week 9 of the 2024 season against the Seattle Seahawks . Watson had four receptions for 65 yards and his career-best eighth touchdown of the season before exiting. Less than a month ago, he left the Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers only to return later with a trip to the hospital in between. Tests showed Watson fractured a rib but suffered no …

stories.title: Christian Watson ruled out with a concussion
stories.summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was disqualified for the hit that injured Watson.
stories.detail: Packers wide receiver Christian Watson will not return for the second half of Wednesday night's game against the Rams. Watson went to the locker room for a concussion evaluation shortly before halftime and the Packers announced that he has been ruled out at the start of the second half. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to his injury. The Rams also lost safety Kamren Kinchens for the rest of the game on the same play. Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson. Rams tight end Davis Allen has also been ruled out with an ankle injury. The two teams went to the break tied 13-13 and that remains the score early in the third quarter.

stories.title: Cowboys fans grade Mike Pettine’s first game calling the defense
stories.summary: Cowboys fans grade Mike Pettine’s first game calling the defense
stories.detail: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Last week there was a big shakeup among the Dallas Cowboys coaching staff. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker wasn’t stripped of his title or fired, but he was stripped of his play-calling duties for the defense. Senior advisor Mike Pettine took over the play-calling, even though he’s only been with the team for a month or so. The Cowboys won their game 51-30 over the Tennessee Titans. We wanted to know how Pettine did in his first go-around calling the Cowboys defense. The fact that Tennessee scored 30 points had some wondering if the change made any difference. Others saw improvement in communication and other areas, even if it didn’t show up as much in the final score. We asked you to grade his performance, and 50% of respondents gave him a middle of the road ‘C’. The next biggest group of votes was 29% for a ‘D’ grade. Suffice it to say, most Cowboys fans came away pretty unimpressed, although a ‘C’ grade is probably as good of a grade as any defensive effort this season, so maybe there was improvement. stories.title: Here's a roadmap to the Aaron Rodgers developments, one of the craziest stories in years
stories.summary: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck.
stories.detail: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck. We've reconstructed the full timeline as to the events regarding now-former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It actually started on Monday, when coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether he has considered using one of the team's other three quarterbacks when the offense is struggling. McCarthy, whose body language in hindsight suggests he was dreading the question , said without equivocation, " Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback ." On Tuesday, Rodgers took his usual reps at practice. He conducted his usual midweek press conference. Unbeknownst to most of the media or the general public, the Steelers were changing their play-calling procedures to have quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, and not McCarthy, communicate the calls to Rodgers through the speaker in his helmet. Then came Tuesday night. At 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers issued a statement — not from coach Mike McCarthy or G.M. teamStories.detail: BEREA, Ohio -- — Deshaun Watson and Fernando Mendoza have plenty to prove when Cleveland hosts Las Vegas on Sunday night. Mendoza, the top overall pick in April's draft, will make his third NFL start and his first in primetime. stories.summary: — Jose Alvarado scored a season-high 21 points, Mikal Bridges had a season-best 19 and the New York Knicks rode a blitz by their bench to a 121-102 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night that extended their winning streak to six.
stories.detail: NEW YORK -- — Jose Alvarado scored a season-high 21 points, Mikal Bridges had a season-best 19 and the New York Knicks rode a blitz by their bench to a 121-102 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night that extended their winning streak to six. Jalen Brunson also scored 19, but the Knicks captain, who was questionable earlier in the day with an illness, labored to a 6-for-22 shooting night and the Knicks fell behind by 11 points multiple times. It was Alvarado, his backup, who was on the floor when the Knicks blew by the Cavaliers to start the fourth quarter. Josh Hart had 15 points, 12 assists and seven rebounds, and Karl-Anthony Towns finished with 12 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists, barely extending his season-opening streak to 17 consecutive games with a double-double. The defending champion Knicks would have been eliminated from NBA Cup title contention with a loss but outscored the Cavs 39-17 in the fourth on their blue court with orange lining the outside. Donovan Mitchell scored 30 points and James Harden had 28 for the Cavaliers, who fell to 9-10. stories.title: Knicks assistant coach Chris Jent returns to team
stories.summary: Chris Jent was back on New York's bench for Wednesday night's NBA Cup win against Cleveland after a monthlong absence.
stories.detail: NEW YORK -- Knicks assistant coach Chris Jent returned to the team Wednesday following a leave of absence . Jent stepped away from the Knicks in late October for an undisclosed reason, shortly after the season began. He was back on the bench for Wednesday night's 121-102 NBA Cup win against the Cleveland Cavaliers . Jent, 56, was a member of Knicks head coach Mike Brown's staff in Cleveland and was on the Charlotte Hornets ' coaching staff in 2024-25. He was the Orlando Magic 's interim coach for 18 games in 2004-05. Jent played at Ohio State from 1988 to 1992.

stories.detail: PHILADELPHIA -- 76ers forward Jaylen Brown exited Wednesday night's 111-104 NBA Cup win against the Miami Heat and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness. Coach Nick Nurse said postgame that Brown would undergo imaging and the team would have an update on his hamstring Thursday. After scoring his sixth point of the night on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed the hamstring, then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points. Brown left that game early because of a hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks . He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness." "You want to make sure you play it the right way, be safe," he said. "Also, don't want to miss a lot of games, so I want to be out there, but also got to be smart. So I think I played it the right way today." Brown is averaging 22.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists on the …

Naz Reid had 18 points, while Moussa Diabate added 14 points and 14 rebounds for the Hornets, who shot 41% from the field. After the New York Knicks became the first team to win the NBA Cup and Finals in the same season, can Jalen Brunson & Co. keep their championship run going?
